item.title: Grid Coordinates and Location Pinpointing
item.explanation: By combining horizontal parallels of latitude and vertical meridians of longitude, every position on Earth can be pinpointed using exact angular coordinates.

item.title: Solar Time and Standard Meridians
item.explanation: Earth rotates 15° longitude per hour (1° every 4 minutes). To prevent temporal confusion, nations establish a central Standard Meridian (e.g. 82.5° E for IST).

item.title: Transformation of Resources via Skill
item.explanation: Economic value addition occurs when human skill, labor, and machinery transform raw materials (e.g. ₹600 wood) into functional products (e.g. ₹1,000 chair).

item.title: Interdependence of Economic Sectors
item.explanation: Primary raw material extraction, secondary manufacturing, and tertiary services form a continuous supply chain where no single sector can function alone.

stages: 1. Primary Stage: Forestry workers harvest timber trees and extract wood pulp from forests.
2. Secondary Stage (Paper Mill): Industrial workers process pulp into large paper rolls.
3. Secondary Stage (Printing Press): Printers bind text and images onto paper to assemble textbooks.
4. Tertiary Stage (Logistics & Distribution): Transport trucks deliver books to warehouses and retail stores.
5. Tertiary Stage (Retail): Bookstores sell finished textbooks directly to students.

item.cause: Earth's rotation from West to East at 15° longitude per hour
item.effect: Places located further East experience sunrise earlier, creating local solar time differences of 4 minutes per degree of longitude.

item.cause: Lack of refrigeration and perishable nature of raw milk in 1940s Anand
item.effect: Milk farmers were forced to sell to private middlemen at unfair low prices, prompting the creation of the AMUL cooperative.

item.cause: Failure of residents to segregate wet and dry household waste at home
item.effect: Municipal waste collection systems clog, recycling efficiency drops, and foul odors and disease risks increase in urban centers.

items: 1. Legislature: Body of elected representatives that formulates, amends, or repeals laws.
2. Executive: Administrative branch headed by PM/CM and civil servants that implements laws.
3. Judiciary: Independent court system that interprets laws and delivers justice.

item.category: The Three Levels of Governance in India
items: 1. National / Central Level: Governs the entire country (headquartered in New Delhi).
2. State Level: Governs individual states (e.g. Karnataka, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu).
3. Local Level: Governs local villages (Panchayats) and urban cities (Municipalities).

item.category: The Three Tiers of Panchayati Raj
items: 1. Gram Panchayat (Base Tier): Village-level elected council headed by a Sarpanch.
2. Panchayat Samiti (Middle Tier): Block-level council coordinating multiple Gram Panchayats.
3. Zila Parishad (Apex Tier): District-level council overseeing regional development.
item.source_context: Chapter 11: Grassroots Democracy – Part 2 (Local Government in Rural Areas) (fees111.pdf)

item.category: The Three Types of Urban Local Bodies
items: 1. Nagar Panchayat: Transitional body governing areas changing from rural to urban.
2. Municipal Council (Nagar Palika): Local body governing smaller towns and medium cities.
3. Municipal Corporation (Nagar Nigam): Local body governing large metropolitan cities.
item.source_context: Chapter 12: Grassroots Democracy – Part 3 (Local Government in Urban Areas) (fees112.pdf)

items: 1. Primary Sector: Natural resource extraction (farming, fishing, mining, forestry).
2. Secondary Sector: Manufacturing, utilities, and construction (factories, mills, power plants).
3. Tertiary Sector: Services, logistics, banking, trade, and retail.
